newsitem.title: JAPAN: Stasco sets 1997 term Oman crude at MPM+11 cents. [CORRECTED 9:36 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Stasco sets 1997 term Oman crude at MPM+11 cents. [CORRECTED 9:36 GMT]

text.p: Shell International Trading and Shipping Co (Stasco) said on Thursday that it had set the term price for the sale of 1997 Oman crude to Asian customers at MPM plus 11 cents.
The level is up three cents (corrects from "two cents") from 1996, when the term price was set at MPM plus eight cents.
Most traders said they considered the premium "quite reasonable".
Asian customers must inform Stasco whether they accept the price or not by Friday morning. There is no further room for negotiation on the price.
In recent years the Stasco premium, which is used as a benchmark price for other term talks concerning Oman sales, has been set at around two cents above the average traded spot premium.
Traders said the average traded spot premium for Oman in 1996 has been 10 to 11 cents.
This led some sources to assess the likely outcome of the price negotiations at MPM plus 12 cents or higher.
One trader said he believed that some term lifters had already accepted the 1997 Stasco price.
